prompt: For independent events A and B, which operation finds P(A and B)?
explanation: P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B) for independent events — multiply along the branches.

prompt: Events A and B are independent: P(A) = 0.3, P(B) = 0.5. Find P(A and B).
Events A and B: P(A) = 0.3, P(B) = 0.5, P(A and B) = 0.15. Find P(A or B).
A bag has 4 red and 6 blue balls. One is picked, replaced, then another is picked. Find P(both red), as a decimal.
workedSolution: With replacement, both picks are independent: $\dfrac{4}{10} \times \dfrac{4}{10} = 0.16$.

prompt: The same bag (4 red, 6 blue) — now two balls are picked WITHOUT replacement. Find P(both red), as a decimal to 3 d.p.
workedSolution: $\dfrac{4}{10} \times \dfrac{3}{9} = \dfrac{12}{90} = 0.133$ (3 d.p.) — the second pick has one fewer red ball and one fewer ball overall.

prompt: Same bag, without replacement. Find P(at least one red), as a decimal to 3 d.p.
workedSolution: $P(\text{no red}) = \dfrac{6}{10}\times\dfrac{5}{9} = \dfrac{30}{90} = \dfrac{1}{3}$, so $P(\text{at least one red}) = 1-\dfrac{1}{3} = 0.667$ (3 d.p.).

prompt: Put these steps in order for finding P(at least one success) in two picks without replacement.
items: Find P(no success) on the first pick
Find P(no success) on the second pick, adjusting for one fewer item
Multiply the two "no success" probabilities together

prompt: A bag has 5 yellow and 3 green counters. Two counters are picked without replacement. Find the probability of exactly one yellow counter.
indicativeContent: Two paths give exactly one yellow: (yellow, green) and (green, yellow)
A full-marks answer identifies both paths, calculates each correctly, and adds them together (not just finds one path)
